In 1914 most of Europe's great powers were at war within weeks. Italy waited until 1915, Romania until 1916, Greece until 1917. One map of who fought in WWI and when they joined.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Blue is the Allies, red the Central Powers, grey neutral, with the year each country joined. Russia, France, the UK, Belgium and Serbia are marked 1914, as are Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire.
2/ Belgium didn't choose. Germany invaded it on 4 August 1914, and Britain declared war on Germany the same day after Belgium asked for help.
3/ Italy is the odd one out. It was a formal member of the Triple Alliance with Germany and Austria-Hungary, yet declared neutrality in 1914 and later joined the Allies.
4/ The Treaty of London, signed 26 April 1915, promised Italy Italian-populated lands held by Austria-Hungary plus concessions in the Balkans. Italy declared war on Austria-Hungary on 23 May 1915.
5/ Romania waited until 27 August 1916, declaring war on Austria-Hungary. It wanted Transylvania, where many people spoke Romanian. Germany declared war on Romania the next day.
6/ Greece was split. King Constantine I favoured neutrality, while Venizelos set up a rival government in Thessaloniki in 1916. Greece formally joined the Allies on 30 June 1917.
Spain and Switzerland sat the whole war out (grey on the map). Which late entry surprised you most? Follow @forummapping for more maps. Borders: HistoGIS (CC BY 4.0)
